concepts.title: The Civilization Cycle as Crowd Cycle
concepts.excerpt: In the years immediately before the Christian era, in Roman Gaul, sixty Gallic cities representing every region of what would later become France pooled their resources and built a temple together at Lyons in honour of the emperor Augustus.

concepts.title: The Functionary Caste and Administrative Tyranny
concepts.excerpt: In 1895, Le Bon describes a form of despotism that did not yet have a name in any major political vocabulary, but that he predicts will outlast every other political form of his century.

concepts.title: Declining Superorganism: Perceptual Shutdown
concepts.excerpt: When a superorganism faces decline that cannot be reversed—when military defeat is inevitable, when economic collapse is in motion, when the structural foundation is crumbling—something strange happens.

concepts.title: Rising Superorganism Hypervigilance: The Paradox of Ascending Power
concepts.excerpt: A superorganism climbing the hierarchy experiences something counterintuitive: the higher it rises, the more threatened it feels.

concepts.title: Cultural Regression Under Stress: Collapse of the Sophisticated
concepts.excerpt: A civilization in expansion phase produces art, philosophy, literature, science, and cultural sophistication.

concepts.title: Learning from History: Breaking Civilizational Cycles Through Knowledge
concepts.excerpt: Civilizations know about the decline of Rome. They study the Ottoman Empire's overextension.

concepts.title: Demographic Collapse: The Parsi Zoroastrian Extinction Timeline
concepts.excerpt: - 1950s-1960s: Approximately 100,000 Parsis in India - 1991 census: 81,600 Parsis - 2001 census: 69,601 Parsis (documented 8% decline in single decade) - 2011 census: ~60,000 Parsis (estimated 13% further decline) - 2024 estimate: ~50,000-60,000 Parsis in India (likely lower)

concepts.title: Tasmania: How Aboriginal Populations Lost Megafauna Hunting
concepts.excerpt: When Australian Aboriginals arrived on Tasmania around 43,000 years ago, the island was populated by megafauna: giant wombats (Diprotodon), 3-meter-tall kangaroos, massive carnivores, and other Pleistocene fauna.

concepts.title: Parsi Zoroastrianism: When Ecology Triggers Religious Extinction
concepts.excerpt: Zoroastrianism is the world's oldest belief system still practiced—origins in pre-Islamic Persia, possibly 1500 BCE or earlier.

concepts.title: Māori Genocide of Moriori: When Pacifism Becomes Strategic Catastrophe
concepts.excerpt: The Chatham Islands, 800 kilometers east of New Zealand, were settled by Polynesian voyagers perhaps 1,000 years before Māori reached the main New Zealand islands.

concepts.title: Arctic Exploration: Failure, Adaptation, and Environmental Determinism
concepts.excerpt: Arctic exploration (19th century attempts to traverse the polar regions, seek the Northwest Passage, reach the North Pole) faced an environment that was actively hostile: - Temperatures below -40°C (-40°F) in winter - Darkness for months (polar night) - Ice pack that moved unpredictably, crushing ships - Scurvy from lack of fresh food - Frostbite and hypothermia from exposure - Psychological stress from isolation and confinement

concepts.title: Franklin Expedition: The Archaeology of Catastrophe
concepts.excerpt: The Franklin Expedition (1845-1848, final survivors until 1859) has occupied the British imagination as a tragedy of epic scale: two ships with 129 men attempting the Northwest Passage, disappearing into the Arctic, their fate unknown for 170 years.

concepts.title: The Bechter Killing & Dignitas Economics
concepts.excerpt: Temüjin kills his half-brother Bechter over a dispute about stolen meat from a hunt.

concepts.title: Endorphin Anesthesia & Comfort-Seeking in Decline
concepts.excerpt: When an animal is cornered—when escape is impossible and threat is inescapable—something shifts in its nervous system.

concepts.title: Technology Lock-In and Path Dependence: Why Past Choices Constrain Future Options
concepts.excerpt: The QWERTY keyboard layout was designed in the 1870s to prevent typewriter jams (high-frequency letter pairs were separated to avoid striking adjacent keys simultaneously).
